sourcedFrom: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A (not printed)
cleanIntro: The International .410 is a gas autoloader that comes apart in four movements: magazine cap and forearm forward, barrel out with the gas piston in its cylinder, bolt out by its operating handle, and the trigger housing down and forward. Two things differ from the bigger Mossberg autoloaders: the barrel comes off with the operating handle drawn HALF WAY back, and the operating handle only pulls out with the action held about a third of the way back. Mossberg International's guide is a thorough cleaning every 200 rounds, sooner in dust, foul weather or with dirty ammunition.

steps.title: Safety button pushed fully to the RIGHT - that is ON
steps.action: The safety is a crossbolt button in the trigger guard. Push it from the left side, the side opposite the ejection port, until it moves all the way to the right and will go no further. That is ON (SAFE); fully left is OFF (FIRE).
steps.prose: All the way, every time. The book warns that a button left part-way between the two positions can leave you believing the gun is on SAFE or FIRE when it is neither, and that pulling the trigger with the safety in that middle position may fire it.
steps.quote: To put the safety in the "ON" (SAFE) position, the safety button must be pushed from the left side (side opposite the ejection port) so that it moves all the way to the right.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — THE MECHANICAL SAFETY, printed p.9 (PDF p.9)

steps.title: Tube first: gun upside down, elevator held, shell stop pressed
steps.action: Safety ON, muzzle safe, fingers nowhere near the trigger. Turn the shotgun so the trigger guard faces up. Hold the elevator down and press the shell stop; one shell comes out of the magazine tube under spring pressure. Repeat until the tube is empty.
steps.prose: If the elevator will not go down, a press of the bolt release button frees it, as the book notes. One shell per press - count them out against what you loaded.
steps.quote: Hold the elevator down (you might need to press the bolt release button to release the elevator) and depress the shell stop (See Figure 7c). This will release one shell from the magazine tube under spring pressure.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.19 (PDF p.19)

steps.title: Then the chamber: gun upright, operating handle fully back, lock it open
steps.action: With the tube empty, turn the gun back upright and pull the operating handle fully to the rear. That ejects the chambered round. Press the bolt lock button and lock the action open.
steps.prose: Tube before chamber is the book's order, so that no shell is fed up from the magazine while you are working the action. Then look into the chamber, at the elevator and into the magazine tube before going on.
steps.quote: With the magazine tube empty (all shotshells removed) rotate the gun to its normal position. Pull the operation handle fully rearward. This will eject the round in the chamber of the firearm
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — UNLOADING THE FIREARM, printed p.19 (PDF p.19)

steps.title: Eye protection on
steps.action: Glasses on before the magazine cap turns.
steps.prose: The book names both hazards: oil spatter and spring-loaded parts.
steps.quote: Wear eye protection during disassembly and cleaning to protect your eyes from oil spatter or spring loaded components.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Check the chamber and magazine once more
steps.action: Look and feel: chamber empty, magazine tube empty.
steps.prose: The book opens the forearm removal with this check even though you have just unloaded. It costs seconds.
steps.quote: Visually and physically check the chamber and magazine to make sure the shotgun is unloaded.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE FOREARM, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Bolt locked back
steps.action: Press the bolt lock button and pull the operating handle back as far as it will go. It should stay locked back.
steps.prose: If it rides forward again, the bolt lock button was not held in - press it and try again.
steps.quote: Depress the bolt lock button (Figure 5), pull the operating handle back as far as it will go
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE FOREARM, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)
steps.warn: The bolt is always under spring pressure.

steps.title: Magazine cap off, counter-clockwise
steps.action: Unscrew the magazine cap counter-clockwise and take it off.
steps.prose: It goes back on finger-tight only, so it should not need a tool to come off.
steps.quote: Unscrew the magazine cap (counterclockwise) and remove it.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE FOREARM, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Forearm forward off the tube
steps.action: Slide the forearm toward the muzzle and off.
steps.prose: Straight forward along the magazine tube.
steps.quote: Slide the forearm toward the muzzle and remove it.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE FOREARM, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Operating handle HALF way back, barrel out
steps.action: Pull the operating handle, and the bolt with it, about half way back. That disengages the bolt from the barrel, and the barrel then pulls straight out of the receiver, gas cylinder sliding forward off the magazine tube.
steps.prose: Half way is the point. Fully locked back or fully forward, the bolt is not where the book says it lets go of the barrel.
steps.quote: pull the operating handle (and the bolt) half way back. This will allow the bolt to be disengaged from the barrel, allowing you to pull the barrel out of the receiver freely.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE BARREL, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Gas piston: in the barrel, or slide it off the tube
steps.action: The gas piston normally comes away in the barrel's gas cylinder. If it stayed on the magazine tube, slide it forward off the tube.
steps.prose: Note which way it faces as it comes off - the book shows a flange, and it has to go back the same way round.
steps.quote: Note: If the gas piston remains on the magazine tube after the barrel is removed, slide the gas piston forward to remove it.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE BARREL, printed p.20 (PDF p.20)

steps.title: Ride the action forward by hand
steps.action: Hold the operating handle, press the bolt release, and ease the action forward until it stops.
steps.prose: Ease it, do not let it go. The bolt is driven forward with considerable force, and the book's unpacking section warns against closing the action with the barrel removed - this controlled ride forward is the one its own disassembly calls for.
steps.quote: Hold the operating handle and depress the bolt release. Ease the action forward until it stops.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE BOLT, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: ⛔ Action held a third back, bolt notch to the handle protrusion, handle straight out
steps.action: Slowly push the action - the bolt action slide and bolt assembly - back about a third of its travel and hold it there. Move the bolt until its notch lines up with the protrusion on the operating handle, then pull the handle straight out.
steps.prose: The handle only clears at that one point. Anywhere else you are levering it against the bolt.
steps.quote: Hold the action in this position and move the bolt to align the bolt notch with the operating handle protrusion
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE BOLT, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Lift the front of the bolt, slide bolt and action bar out forward
steps.action: With the handle out, lift the front of the bolt off the action bar with a finger and slowly slide the bolt and action bar forward until both are clear of the receiver.
steps.prose: The lift is what lets the bolt slide out of the receiver; without it, it hangs up.
steps.quote: Lift the front of the bolt using your finger and slowly slide the bolt and action bar forward until they are completely removed from the receiver.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE BOLT, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Trigger housing pin: tap from the left, out the right
steps.action: Push out the trigger housing retaining pin with a blunt object no larger than 1/8" in diameter, tapping it from the left side and taking it out from the right.
steps.prose: Blunt and small. It goes back in from the right side, flush with the receiver.
steps.quote: Push out the trigger housing retaining pin using a blunt object no larger than 1/8" diameter (See Figure 12). Remove the pin by tapping from the left side, removing it from the right side.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Trigger housing forward and down - and it stays in one piece
steps.action: Press the bolt release button and slide the trigger housing assembly forward and down out of the receiver.
steps.prose: That is as far as the trigger group goes. The book says the housing is a complex assembly that is not to be taken apart; its disassembly belongs to an authorized service center or a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger housing assembly by pushing the bolt release button and sliding the trigger housing assembly forward and down.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)
steps.warn: The trigger housing assembly is a complex assembly and must not be disassembled.

steps.title: ⛔ Do not drop the hammer with the housing out
steps.action: Leave the trigger alone while the housing is out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The hammer is cocked when the housing comes out, and that is how it should stay until the housing is back in the gun.
steps.quote: Do not pull the trigger and allow the hammer to fall when the trigger housing assembly is removed from the receiver. To do so may result in personal injury or damage to the assembly.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Forearm, barrel with its gas piston, operating handle, bolt and action bar, and the trigger housing are all out. The book stops here.
steps.prose: Anything further is gunsmith or service-center work, in the book's own words.
steps.quote: Field disassembly is now complete. Further disassembly should only be performed by a qualified gunsmith or the Product Service Center.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — REMOVING THE TRIGGER HOUSING ASSEMBLY, printed p.21 (PDF p.21)

steps.title: Piston out, then bore, chamber and gas cylinder bore
steps.action: Take the gas piston out of the barrel's gas cylinder. Scrub the bore, the chamber and the gas cylinder bore with solvent, then patches until barrel and gas cylinder bore come clean.
steps.prose: A stiff brass bristle brush shifts stubborn deposits. Finish with a few drops of light oil in the gas cylinder bore and a lightly oiled patch through the bore and chamber - and leave no patch, and no excess oil or grease, behind in the bore.
steps.quote: Scrub the bore of the barrel, chamber and gas cylinder bore with solvent and follow with cleaning patches until barrel and gas cylinder bore are clean.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — BARREL CLEANING, printed p.22 (PDF p.22)

steps.title: Choke tube in while the barrel is cleaned
steps.action: Keep a choke tube properly installed while you clean the bore so residue does not build up on the threads. Keep the tube's own threads clean and lightly oiled.
steps.prose: Never fire the gun without a choke tube in; the book warns it damages the threads inside the barrel.
steps.quote: During cleaning of the barrel, be certain a choke tube is properly installed. This will avoid residue build-up on threads.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — CHOKE TUBES, printed p.26 (PDF p.26)

steps.title: Magazine tube, piston, ring, seal and return spring in solvent
steps.action: Clean the gas system - magazine tube, gas piston, piston ring, seal and the gas action return spring - thoroughly with solvent.
steps.prose: These are the parts that decide whether the gun cycles. The book's tool for stubborn deposits here is a stiff brass bristle brush.
steps.quote: The gas system includes the magazine tube, gas piston, piston ring, seal, and the gas action return spring (See exploded view). These parts should be thoroughly cleaned using solvent.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — GAS SYSTEM CLEANING, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Bolt and slide in an evaporating solvent, oil kept sparing
steps.action: Clean every part of the action, bolt assembly and bolt action slide included, with an evaporating solvent. Lubricate sparingly.
steps.prose: Sparing oil keeps the action cleaner for longer; a wet action collects residue.
steps.quote: Clean all components of the action including the bolt assembly and bolt action slide to remove accumulated residue. An evaporating solvent should be used. Action parts will remain cleaner longer if lubrication is used sparingly.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — ACTION CLEANING, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Receiver tracks clean, a few drops of oil
steps.action: Clean the inside of the receiver with a rag or soft bristle brush, paying special attention to the tracks that guide the bolt and slide, then put a few drops of light oil in those tracks.
steps.prose: Soft bristles only on the receiver and the trigger housing - the book warns a metal-bristle brush can remove their protective coating.
steps.quote: attention to the tracks which guide the bolt and slide. Place a few drops of light oil in these tracks when clean.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — RECEIVER CLEANING, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: Trigger housing brushed, soft bristles only
steps.action: Brush the loose residue off the trigger housing with a soft bristle brush.
steps.prose: Brush it, do not take it apart, and do not pull the trigger while it is out of the receiver.
steps.quote: Brush loose residue from trigger housing with a soft bristle brush.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — TRIGGER HOUSING CLEANING, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

steps.title: A light coat of oil, then wiped back with a dry cloth
steps.action: Give all metal parts a light coat of gun oil, then wipe them thoroughly with a dry cloth.
steps.prose: Wipe it back. Excess oil speeds carbon build-up in the gas system and can hurt how the gun runs.
steps.quote: Apply a light coat of gun oil to all metal parts and then wipe thoroughly with a dry cloth.
steps.cite: MOSSBERG INTERNATIONAL 410 GAUGE AUTOLOADING SHOTGUN OWNERS MANUAL — Mossberg International 410 gauge autoloading shotgun owner's manual, PART NO. 104572 REV. A — GAS SYSTEM CLEANING, printed p.23 (PDF p.23)

deepAbsentReason: The International .410 book ends at field disassembly. After the trigger housing comes out it says field disassembly is now complete and that further disassembly should only be performed by a qualified gunsmith or the Product Service Center (printed p.21); on the same page it states the trigger housing assembly must not be disassembled. Everything the book publishes - forearm, barrel and gas piston, operating handle, bolt and action bar, and the trigger housing - is walked in the field strip. Nothing deeper is published, so nothing deeper is walked.

cleaning.name: BARREL & GAS CYLINDER
tasks: Gas piston out of the barrel's gas cylinder
Bore, chamber and gas cylinder bore scrubbed with solvent, then patches until clean
A stiff brass bristle brush on stubborn deposits
A few drops of light oil in the gas cylinder bore; a final lightly oiled patch through the bore and chamber
Choke tube installed while the bore is cleaned; its threads kept clean and lightly oiled
⛔ Never leave a cleaning patch, or excess oil or grease, in the bore
Never fire the shotgun without a choke tube properly installed

cleaning.name: GAS SYSTEM
tasks: Magazine tube, gas piston, piston ring, seal and gas action return spring cleaned in solvent
A stiff brass bristle brush on stubborn deposits

cleaning.name: BOLT & ACTION
tasks: Bolt assembly and bolt action slide cleaned with an evaporating solvent
Lubricate sparingly - action parts stay cleaner longer

cleaning.name: RECEIVER & TRIGGER HOUSING
tasks: Inside of the receiver with a rag or soft bristle brush, the bolt and slide tracks especially
A few drops of light oil in the tracks once clean
Trigger housing: loose residue brushed off with a soft bristle brush
Never use a metal-bristle brush on the receiver or trigger housing
Do not pull the trigger with the trigger housing out of the receiver
Do not disassemble the trigger housing assembly

cleaning.name: OIL & STORAGE
tasks: A light coat of gun oil on all metal parts, wiped thoroughly with a dry cloth
Avoid over-lubrication below freezing
For long storage clean and oil thoroughly; do not plug the barrel or store in a fabric-lined case

reassembly: No ammunition anywhere near the bench; chamber and magazine tube stay empty. Eye protection on.
Trigger housing: press the bolt release button while pushing the housing up and rearward into the receiver; push the pin into the hole on the right side until it is flush with the receiver.
Bolt assembly onto the bolt action slide, and the slide onto the magazine tube.
Slowly push the slide into the receiver. Looking through the ejection port, line up the notch in the slide with the notch in the bolt, then fit the operating handle into the bolt assembly.

Barrel: check the gas piston is in the barrel's gas cylinder the right way round, slide the barrel into the receiver with the gas cylinder on the magazine tube, then pull the operating handle half way back to seat the barrel fully.
Forearm: press the bolt lock button and pull the operating handle back so the action stays open, slide the forearm over the magazine tube and seat it into the receiver.
Magazine cap onto the front of the magazine tube, finger-tight.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Safety ON - fully to the right - and prove the chamber, elevator and magazine tube empty, muzzle somewhere safe throughout. Pull the bolt fully back: it should lock open. Fingers clear of the ejection port, press the bolt release: the bolt should run forward and lock fully closed; repeat several times to feel the action move freely. Action closed, safety ON: pull the trigger fully - the hammer should NOT fall. Finger off, safety to OFF - fully left - and the hammer should still not fall. Pull the trigger: the hammer should fall. Open the action and put the safety back ON. If any step does not behave as described, the book says not to load or use the gun and to contact the Product Service Center immediately.
